findings.cs_reference: GCSViews/ConfigurationView/ConfigRawParams.cs:237-252 (data[name] = double.Parse(cell text) in the current culture); ExtLibs/Utilities/ParamFile.cs:85-107 (double.Parse(paramlist[item].ToString()) in the current culture, so the Hashtable's double round-trips through the same culture)
findings.summary: paramfile::save passes format_value(v) as the C# 'ToString()' text. format_value always uses '.', but write_param_lines re-parses it with current-culture double.Parse (AllowThousands). In a culture such as de-DE, normalize_number treats '.' as a group separator, so 0.135 is saved as 135 and 1.5 as 15. Every fractional parameter in the file is corrupted silently. The C# never has this problem because the Hashtable holds a double whose ToString and Parse use the same culture. An exception (e.g. an unparsable value) makes save() log and return an empty string, which the callers then write as an empty file; the C# StreamWriter would have written the lines before the bad one. format_value ({:.7} trimmed, not the grid cell's text) is still also the displayed value everywhere.
findings.required_fix: Give write_param_lines the double the C# Hashtable holds (change the list to (String, f64) and drop the re-parse, or format with double_to_string() in the current culture before calling it). Keep the partial text on an exception, as the C# file would. Model the ConfigRawParams cell text (the value's ToString) instead of format_value, and add a test under a ',' culture.

findings.cs_reference: GCSViews/FlightPlanner.cs:5613-5635 (processToScreen: cell.Value = temp.p1 * multipliers[0] with multipliers a double[], so float params and alt become doubles whose ToString() is G15 of the widened float), 1138-1145 (setfromMap: Lat/Lon cells = lat.ToString("0.0000000")), 6141-6181 (savewaypoints re-parses each cell's ToString())
findings.summary: write_waypoint_file applies one model to every row: float fields go through G7 text and lat/lng through G15. In C# the cell text depends on how the row was filled. Rows from a loaded file or a download are processToScreen doubles, so p1 = 45.3f saves as 45.29999924 and alt 45.3f as 45.299999 (the R61-08 'expected' 45.30000000 only holds for typed cells). Rows added on the map hold lat/lng as 7-decimal strings, so C# saves -35.36326120 where Rust saves -35.36326123. The home fallback line is chosen from (0,0) instead of an empty TXT_homelat, so a home at exactly 0,0 writes the fallback instead of the 16 line. The same cell model also affects what the C# uploads (7-decimal lat/lng for map-added points).
findings.required_fix: Model the Commands grid as cell values with their C# types (string for typed and setfromMap cells, double for processToScreen cells, int for setfromMap alt) and have savewaypoints and the upload paths read the cell's ToString(). Until then, record per row whether it came from processToScreen or setfromMap and format accordingly. Track 'home text empty' explicitly. Add golden-text tests for each source.

findings.cs_reference: Swarm/Formation.cs:84-324 (the try covers the transform and the send; the catch prints 'Failed to send command' and nothing is sent to that follower); Swarm/FormationControl.cs getOffsetFromLeader (no catch: the exception leaves the handler)
findings.summary: R61-11's transform is fixed, but the error paths are new divergences that matter for safety. target_for returns the leader's own lat/lng/alt when ProjNet throws, and follower_command then sends a position target at the leader's position. C# sends nothing for that follower. offset_from_leader returns (0, 0, 0) on an exception; update_positions accepts it (|x|, |y| < 200) and overwrites the follower's stored offset with zero, so later targets also coincide with the leader. In C# the exception escapes and no offset is stored. The doc comment at swarm.rs:166-167 states the C# behaviour wrongly.
findings.required_fix: Return Result/Option from target_for and offset_from_leader; skip the follower's command on Err (log 'Failed to send command ...'), and do not update the offset on Err. Fix the doc comments.

findings.cs_reference: GCSViews/FlightPlanner.cs:3272-3299 (enterUTMCoordToolStripMenuItem_Click: int.Parse/double.Parse in the current culture, new UTM(zoneint, e, n, Hemisphere.South) from GeoUtility, (Geographic)utm, Commands.Rows.Add, updateUndoBuffer(false), setfromMap(lat, lng, (int)ans.Alt))
findings.summary: Enter UTM Coord converts with utmpos.ToLLA (ProjNet) through utm_to_latlng, where the C# uses GeoUtility's UTM->Geographic series. The parsers are Rust str::parse (invariant, no AllowThousands), and a bad entry returns silently where int.Parse/double.Parse throw. setfromMap is called with alt (int)ans.Alt = 0 in C#; Rust uses new_wp's default altitude.
findings.required_fix: Use GeoUtility UTM::new(zone, e, n, Hemisphere::South) and to_geographic(), parse with dotnet::int_parse/double_parse, surface the exception, and pass alt 0 to the setfromMap equivalent.

verdict: A solid fix round for the map and file paths, with no definite compile errors. The wp route now has Mission Planner's direction arrows, an unset home no longer draws a leg to 0,0, spline points lose Alt/Tag as in C#, and .plan/.waypoints loading follows LoadWPFile, readQGC110wpfile and a close processToScreen port with the Reset Home prompt. ParamFile saving and Formation's transform are wired. New problems: the param save re-parses '.' text in the current culture and corrupts fractional values in comma-decimal locales; the WPL writer's single numeric model does not match the C# grid's per-source cell text; swarm's exception paths now command followers to the leader's position; and FENCE/RALLY downloads, the context Save WP File, the fence/rally loaders and setWPParams still bypass the C# code. No new owned files were ported, so progress stays at about 5.5% (26,127 / 479,014) and the cap stays 1.6. Awarded 1.3; round-file fidelity 6.2; UI/UX 2.2; features 3.0.
